answer: An operator copying one text across 192 aliases as a result pays for 192 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. Since the hollow hash is stored at intake, the knoll graph groups the endorsements and the crystal audit exposes the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 2 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
